en: Wait... Don't tell me you're going commando right now!?
I... I beg your pardon!? I can't answer that!
Oh, don't be silly. Of course you know the answer.
Did you maybe have an accident? Couldn't find a restroom nearby? I can sympathize. Been there, done that, hahaha.
You're disgusting...
What, it's nothing to be ashamed of. Everyone's whipped up some underwear curry at least once in their lifetime, right? Some people do it all the time!
Ahem!

What is your problem, Ta-chan!? Be professional!
Can't you see you're making her uncomfortable!?
Oh, ah, forgive me. I have a twisted sense of humor, you see...
Should I warm up this underwear for you?
Excuse me? You want to... warm it up?

Well, it's just that it's so cold out. I thought maybe you
would rather slip on something warm and toasty.
But... how would you go about doing that?
Oh, right, the microwave probably won't do the trick. I know. I'll stick it under my shirt and warm it against my skin.
I really don't think you need to go that far...
Are you sure? You are going to put this on here, aren't you?
No! I'm going to take it home!
Sorry... I was only trying to help.
(What would you need to say to someone buying underwear? Can't think of anything in particular.)
Um, excuse me? Is something wrong?
Oh, no, nothing at all. Sorry, it's just that today's my first day.
Oh, is that right? Then good luck! I'm sure you'll get the hang of it. ♪
Oh, wow, haha. Thank you very much!
(Wow. What a nice lady. Boy am I glad I didn't say anything stupid.)
(No, there's nothing you need to ask someone buying underwear. What am I thinking?)
Oh, and may I also have some cigarettes?
Cigarettes? Certainly. One pack?
(Cigarettes, huh? Oh, before I can sell these, I have to confirm one thing.)
Excuse me, but may I check your gender, please?
What a question to ask! You should be ashamed of yourself.
I'm sorry, miss. But before I can sell you any tobacco, I'm required to check your gender. It's the law.
Wait a minute... Aren't you confusing it with having to check my age? To make sure I'm not a minor?
Oh. Right. Of course! Haha, how stupid of me...
Excuse me, but may I check your age, please?
Oh, yes, that's right. Will my driver's license do?
(Hey, I'm starting to get the hang of this after all.)
Excuse me, but may I check you for tattoos, please?
I beg your pardon? I have never had any done. Why would you even want to know?
I'm sorry, but before I can sell you any tobacco, I'm required to check you for tattoos. It's the law.
But that's something only hot springs care about... Are you maybe confusing it with checking my age, to make sure I'm not a minor?
Uh... Right! Yes, that's it! I'm so sorry...
Before I can sell you these cigarettes, I think I'm supposed to check something...
Something like my age, maybe? To make sure I'm not a minor?
How much do I owe you?
Uh, your total comes out to 1,127 yen.
I don't have anything small. Oh, but I do have 7 yen in change. Here's 10,007 yen.
Then your change comes out to 8,880 yen.
Oh, I'm sorry. I found 20 more yen.
(Not again! Things are getting complicated...)
(Okay, for a sale of 1,127 yen, she gave me 10,007 yen and then 20 yen more. That means the change should be...)
Your change comes to 9,900 yen.
Thank you. Oh, and I don't need a bag. I have my handbag.
Great. Thank you for shopping with us.
(Huh? Wait, did I get the math right? For merchandise totaling 1,127 yen, she gave me 10,007 yen and then 20 more.)
(That's 10,007 yen plus 20 yen minus 1,127 yen. So, that's 10,027 yen minus 1,127 yen. Meaning the change should be... 8,900 yen!)
(Dang it! I gave her too much change!)
Hey, Ta-chan!

en: Sorry! I didn't mean to! Change is just so tricky, you know?
Your change comes out to 8,900 yen.
Great! Thank you for shopping with us!

(Being a convenience store clerk takes a lot more thought
than I expected... Man, this is exhausting.)
What!? What is it!? I'm doing my job, aren't I!?
Your change comes out to 9,800 yen.
Um, are you okay?
Oh, I'm sorry. I'm still struggling with the math.
(Um, for merchandise totaling 1,127 yen, she gave me 10,007 yen and then 20 more. So, her change should be...)
Huh!? Was that the⑬
The shoplifter! It's him! Ta-chan, chase down him, quick!
So he's finally reared his ugly, thieving head... Okay, I'm on it!
I've never worked in a convenience store before. Are you sure this'll be okay?
I'll back you up if you run into any trouble. It shouldn't be too bad.
You just need to think on your feet. For instance, if someone's buying a bento, you need to give them chopsticks or a fork.
You need to observe and think about what the customer needs, and respond quickly and appropriately.
Let's give it a try. Say I were to buy one of these. What does this item need?
(It's a juice carton. So, the customer would need...)
A straw.

Bingo. Now, this kind of situation arises all the time.
I know⑬it's complicated. But you need to make decisions
each time about how you can best help the customer.

If you can't even figure out their basic convenience store
needs, they'll get really pissy with you. So staying on your
toes is a must.
Oh, I'm sure I can at least do that.
Okay then. I'm going to be on the floor keeping an eye out for that shoplifter. If I spot him, I'll give you a holler.
All right, Ta-chan, I think that just about sums it up. I'll be counting on you!
A cup?
No, you don't want to be <Italic>that</Italic> generous. We'd go bankrupt if we gave out cups with every drink.
A pair of chopsticks.
You don't need chopsticks to drink juice. Have you ever seen anyone at a convenience store do that?
Too slow, Ta-chan! You have to decide more quickly.
Oh. Okay. Dang, I have to be faster than I thought.
A straw is the right choice here, but you'll have to make complicated decisions like this each and every time. I know⑬it can be very taxing on the mind.

But if you can't even figure out their basic convenience

Okay. Damn, this sounds kind of challenging.
Don't worry. I'm going to be on the floor keeping an eye out for that shoplifter. If I spot him, I'll give you a holler.
(Okay. I'll just focus on manning the counter.)
(My first customer already. What's he buying?)
I'll take this.
(Pasta, huh? What should I ask him?)
Party of one, sir?
Huh? Well, yeah, it's just me. But why does that even matter?
Uh, no reason. No reason at all.
(Yikes! I think I screwed up!)
Normally, you should be asking me if I wanted my pasta heated up, right?
Oh, right! Yes, yes. Should I warm your pasta?
That's what I just said! I'm in a hurry here, so can you speed it up?
(Sheesh. Why do customers have to be such jerks?)
Should I microwave this for you?
Yeah, please.
(Oh, yeah, this is easy. Just need to keep it up.)
Should I pour some hot water in there?
Huh? Hot water for pasta? What are you saying? It's not cup ramen, you know.
Normally, you should be asking me if I wanted my pasta heated, right?
Hey, what are you doing? Hurry it up.
Microwave my pasta, and make it snappy. Can't you see I'm in a hurry?
(Oh, that's right. Come on, Tatsuo, don't let this get you down.)
(Oh, hang on. Pasta's not a finger food. So the customer needs...)
I'll put a spoon in the bag.
What? Why? Can you eat pasta with a spoon?
Er, can't you?
Most people use a fork, right? Chopsticks maybe, but a spoon? Not likely.
Oh, but you see people using spoons sometimes. They take a fork and put the pasta on a spoon, and...
They're still using a fork! Now look, you can't eat pasta with just a spoon. Quit arguing and give me a fork!
(You don't have to lose your temper, man...)
I'll put your straw in the bag.
What? Why? It's pasta. You want me to suck it through a straw?
Why, do you not want to?
Are you nuts!? You're supposed to give me a fork!
Oh. You are so right. Haha, I guess I screwed up.
What's wrong with you?
I'll put a fork in the bag.
Uh-huh. Please do.
(Good. Got it right.)
Hey, wake up. Can you possibly go any slower?
Um... What?
That pasta. I need a fork to eat it, so don't forget to include one.
Oh, right! Yes, absolutely.
Save your breath and get busy. Get it together, man.
So? How much?
Uh, it's 382 yen.
Okay... Crap, I don't have enough change. Here you go, 10,002 yen.
Your change will be 9,620 yen.
Oh, hey, sorry. I actually got 80 yen here.
I'm saying I'll give you 80 yen more, so give me the change from that.
Huh? So, that'll mean the change should be...
Your change will be 9,600 yen.
No, that's not right. Did you calculate it?
Did... Did I get it wrong? Um, let's see...
(For pasta costing 382 yen, he gave me 10,002 yen, and then 80 yen more. That means his change should be...)
Your change will be 9,700 yen.
Okay. Oh, I don't need the receipt.
(That's how it goes, huh? I guess I can manage this.)
Your change will be 10,300 yen.
Oh. Okay. Thanks, dude. I don't need the receipt.
(Huh? Did I get that calculation right? For pasta costing 382 yen, he gave me 10,002 yen, and then 80 yen more.)
(So, that's 10,002 yen plus 80 yen minus 382 yen. That's 10,082 yen minus 382 yen, so the change is... 9,700 yen!)
(Dang it! I gave the guy too much change!)
Something the matter, Ta-chan?
Oh, no... Okay, yes. I gave a customer too much change.
Oh. Yeah, rookies are prone to doing that. Don't bust a vein over it.
Oh, whew! That's a big relief.
Yeah, we just take the difference out of your pay.
Seriously...?
How long does it take you to do a simple calculation? Give me 10,300 yen in change.
Sorry. Here's your change, 10,300 yen.
Okay. Thanks, dude. I don't need the receipt.
(Damn it! He conned me! I gave him too much change!)
Greetings, sir.
(A grandpa this time. What's he got?)
May I have this, please?
(A curry bento. So, I should be asking him...)
Sir, can you really afford that?
Eh? Of course I can! What gives you the gumption to ask such a question!?
Oh, uh, I was just worried whether you had enough money.
That's none of your concern. What nerve!
Yeah... That was pretty callous of me. My bad!
Pardon me for saying this, but don't those contain an awful lot of sodium?
Huh? Oh, perhaps so, but I quite like it. Thank you for your concern, though. That's very considerate of you.
Oh, no, not a problem, sir. But you need to watch your diet. You'll get sick if you only eat convenience store bentos. They're sodium-heavy and chock-full of preservatives.
Isn't there someone around to monitor your nutrition?
Of course there is⑬ No, that's not right. My... She...
Hrk! *sniffle*
Sir, is everything okay? Why are you crying?

My wife, she died recently, and the children live far away.
I... *sob* I have no one left to talk to...
I'm so sorry... I shouldn't have pried.
Should I warm this up, sir?
Ah, yes, please.
I'll put the spoon in the bag as well.
How kind of you. Thank you so much.
Oh, no thanks necessary, sir. Happy to do my job.
(I think I'm getting the hang of this. Guess it's not so bad after all.)
Is something wrong, young man?
Oh, no sir. I'm trying to decide what to do.
Well, let's start with heating the curry. And please don't forget that I'll need a spoon to eat it.
Oh, right. I'm sorry for not noticing.

Come to think of it, I haven't seen you before. Are you a
new hire? Stick with it and you'll eventually learn the
ropes.
Right, thank you.
(Sheesh, even this old grandpa's taking pity on me. I need to get it together.)
Oh, also, I'll take a Steamed Bun, please.
One Steamed Bun? Okay.
And some Bean Paste Buns. I'll take three.
Uh, okay.
Oh, and some Pizza Buns. Two, please. Oh, and cancel one of the Bean Paste Buns. That will do.
(Huh? So, how many of what buns?)
So, your order is one Steamed, two Bean, and two Pizza Buns?
Yes, yes. Good job remembering all that. Well done.
Oh, no, sir. It's nothing special. After all, it is my job.
(Whew. I guess I got that right.)
So, your order is two Steamed, one Bean, and two Pizza Buns?
No, that's wrong. I asked for one Steamed, two Bean, and two Pizza Buns.
Sorry about that, sir...
So, your order is one Steamed, two Bean, and three Pizza Buns?
Sorry about that, sir.
Is something wrong?
I, uh, couldn't keep track of your order. Sorry, but could you repeat that again?
Why certainly. First, I asked for one Steamed Bun. And then, uh... what was it now?
(If you don't say it quickly, I'll forget!)
